Vendor registrations with complete remediation reasons

A CSV reader preserving explicit empty strings feeds this two-destination Reformat. Vendor support reviews the raw source values on output 1, while output 0 loads a typed onboarding application. The receiving teams reconcile using vendor_row, so every source submission must remain traceable.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. A vendor registration goes to the accepted loader on output 0 only when its reference, invoice ceiling, activation date and payment term all satisfy the checks below. Evaluate all four checks independently; one invalid field must not prevent other failed checks being reported.
2. The non-null vendor_ref_no is invalid when trimming leaves nothing. Preserve its original spelling, even outer spaces, in either destination; duplicate references describe separate source submissions rather than a request to merge registrations.
3. Trim invoice_limit_txt. Null, empty and whitespace fail. Accept one to twelve ASCII integer digits, optionally a decimal point and one or two fractional digits. Reject signs, exponents, currency symbols, grouping separators and a trailing decimal point. Zero is valid.
4. Trim activation_dt_txt and accept exactly yyyy-MM-dd or yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss with strict calendar validity in UTC. Null and blank, impossible dates, shortened digits and trailing characters fail. Date-only means midnight; retain supplied timestamp seconds.
5. Trim and uppercase payment_term_txt. Only NET30 and NET60 pass. Null or blank is invalid, while lowercase or surrounding whitespace around a recognized term is valid. Do not normalize the original source field itself.
6. For accepted rows copy every input field unchanged and set approved_amount, effective_dt and business_code from the validated values. Nullable address and contact fields retain null versus empty, and vendor_ledger is an unrelated amount that must survive.
7. Send any failing row exclusively to output 1, copying every original field and adding reject_reason with REF, LIMIT, DATE and TERM for every applicable failure in that order, joined by semicolons without spaces or a trailing separator.
8. Retain arrival order separately within the two destinations. The first and last source submission use the same rules as intervening rows. An invalid value must reach remediation without being converted, and every source row has exactly one destination.

rubric.description: Vendor registrations with complete remediation reasons

required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for accepted rows (written to $out.0) and 1 for rejected rows (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Returning OK/ALL or a single port for every row breaks the accepted/remediation split.

required.check: All four checks (REF, LIMIT, DATE, TERM) are evaluated for every row and each failure is recorded (e.g. appended to a list or separate flags), with no early return or else-if chain after the first failure; a row failing all four yields all four codes.
required.rationale: Stopping at the first failure turns REF;LIMIT;DATE;TERM into REF only.

required.check: Null, empty and whitespace-only invoice_limit_txt fail LIMIT without an exception (nvl/null check before trim and the pattern test; `str2decimal("")` throws).
required.rationale: An unguarded trim/str2decimal on null or empty text throws instead of reporting LIMIT.

required.check: The LIMIT grammar caps the integer part at 12 digits: 1234567890123 (13 digits) fails, 999999999999.99 passes (e.g. whole-string `~= "[0-9]{1,12}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"` or matches()).
required.rationale: A plain numeric test or str2decimal success accepts the 13-digit ceiling.

required.check: The LIMIT grammar is a whole-string match on the trimmed text that rejects a trailing decimal point ("1."), exponents ("1e2"), signs, currency symbols and grouping separators; it uses `~=` or matches(), not the substring operator `?=`, and not "str2decimal succeeds" (which accepts 1e2 / 1.).
required.rationale: Conversion-based validation accepts 1e2 and 1., which the spec rejects.

required.check: Impossible dates (2025-02-30) and shortened digits (2025-1-1) fail DATE via a strict check: either strict `isDate(d, pattern, ..., "UTC", true)`, a strict `str2date(...) : null` conditional-fail, or a regex shape check plus strict isDate (strict isDate alone is verified to reject both).
required.rationale: Lenient parsing rolls 2025-02-30 into March and accepts 2025-1-1.

required.check: Trailing characters ("2026-01-01x") fail DATE through an explicit whole-string shape check (regex such as `[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}( [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})?` with `~=`, or an equivalent length-plus-pattern test); strict isDate/str2date alone is not verified to reject trailing text.
required.rationale: Without a shape check, parsers that stop at the pattern end can accept 2026-01-01x.

required.check: Both yyyy-MM-dd and yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss are accepted, with the parse pattern chosen by the value's shape (or length); a supplied timestamp keeps its seconds in effective_dt (2026-02-28 12:34:56).
required.rationale: Parsing only the date-only pattern rejects valid timestamps or drops the time part.

required.check: effective_dt is parsed with the "UTC" time-zone argument (e.g. `str2date(d, p, "en.US", "UTC", true)`), so a date-only value becomes 00:00:00 UTC; date functions without a time zone use the host zone (CET).
required.rationale: Parsing in the host zone shifts date-only values by an hour in the UTC output field.

required.check: payment_term_txt is compared after trim and upperCase (null-safe, e.g. `upperCase(trim(nvl(x,"")))`): " net30 " passes, null/blank/"bad" fail TERM; business_code receives the normalized value while the source payment_term_txt field is left unchanged.
required.rationale: Comparing the raw text rejects " net30 "; normalizing in place corrupts the copied source field.

required.check: Accepted rows copy all input fields unchanged (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*;` or per-field), including vendor_ref_no with its outer spaces and the raw invoice/date/term texts, and set approved_amount from the validated trimmed limit, effective_dt and business_code.
required.rationale: Copying trimmed values or omitting the copy loses the original spelling the receiving teams reconcile on.

required.check: Rejected rows copy all input fields and set reject_reason to the failed codes in the order REF, LIMIT, DATE, TERM joined by ";" without spaces or a trailing separator (`join(";", list)` or equivalent concatenation); a whitespace-only vendor_ref_no (trim leaves "") yields REF.
required.rationale: Wrong order, spaces or a trailing ; breaks the remediation codes.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2decimal/str2date is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2decimal("") and strict str2date on 2025-02-30 throw, failing the graph instead of routing the row to remediation.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP or ALL (or writes both $out.0 and $out.1 and returns ALL) for some rows, so a row is dropped or reaches both destinations.
forbidden.rationale: Every source row must reach exactly one destination; SKIP drops it and ALL duplicates it.

rubric_notes: Clause 4 trailing-character rejection stays an explicit shape-check item because strict isDate on trailing text is unverified. Old T44.2/T44.8 overlap removed: independence is .2, reason format is .12.

user_message:
Clinic appointment enrollment gate

A community clinic receives enrollment CSV files from several partner practices. The Reformat separates appointments from corrections. Guardianship and program eligibility depend on the same age, but malformed age must not provoke a parsing exception or a fictitious missing-guardian complaint.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Process every clinic enrollment into exactly one destination: output 0 schedules the patient; output 1 requests correction. An enrollment is schedulable only if age, consent, visit day and program checks all pass. Collect independent defects instead of stopping at the first problem.
2. age_txt must be trimmed ASCII digits with one to three characters, then an integer between 0 and 120 inclusive. Null, empty, signed, decimal or exponent forms are invalid. For invalid age do not attempt a conversion and do not apply the dependent guardian rule.
3. For valid ages under 18 a trimmed nonempty guardian_id is required; null and blank fail. For ages 18 or older guardian_id is not validated, even when null. Retain the raw guardian value; adult rows must never acquire a guardian defect.
4. Trim and uppercase consent_txt. Y means consented. N, null, blank and unknown text all fail consent. Consent is an independent requirement for adults and minors; do not infer it from the presence of a guardian.
5. visit_day_txt must have the exact yyyy-MM-dd shape and be a real UTC calendar date between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30 inclusive. The text is not trimmed: surrounding whitespace, null, blank, time-bearing strings and shortened date digits fail; accepted dates are represented at midnight.
6. Normalize program_txt by trimming and uppercase. WELL accepts any valid age; SENIOR requires a valid age of at least 65. Every other code fails. When age is invalid SENIOR fails too, but WELL introduces no additional program defect solely because age was invalid.
7. Accepted output preserves all source fields, adding patient_age, appointment_day and normalized_program. Rejected output preserves the same raw fields with correction_codes containing AGE, GUARDIAN, CONSENT, VISIT and PROGRAM in that order for all applicable defects, separated by commas.
8. Keep source order per destination and retain repeated enrollment_id values. The first and last enrollment can be minors or invalid records; nothing is suppressed. Null clinic_note differs from an empty note and clinic_ledger has no role in eligibility.

rubric.description: Clinic appointment enrollment gate

required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for schedulable rows (written to $out.0) and 1 for correction rows (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Any other return scheme loses or duplicates enrollments.

required.check: Age, guardian, consent, visit and program defects are all collected for every row (no early return after the first defect); e.g. age 1e2 with null consent, 2026-02-30 and SENIOR yields AGE,CONSENT,VISIT,PROGRAM.
required.rationale: Stopping early reports AGE only for a multi-defect row.

required.check: age_txt is validated before conversion as trimmed whole-string 1–3 ASCII digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,3}"`); null, empty, signed, decimal and exponent forms ("1e2") fail AGE and str2integer is not called for them.
required.rationale: Converting first throws on 1e2 or empty text.

required.check: A grammatically valid age is accepted only between 0 and 120 inclusive: 121 fails AGE, 0 is a valid (minor) age.
required.rationale: Off-by-one bounds misclassify 0 or 121.

required.check: For a valid age under 18, a null or whitespace-only guardian_id (trimmed, null-safe) produces GUARDIAN; age 0 with null guardian yields GUARDIAN.
required.rationale: Testing only null misses " "; testing only blank throws or misses null.

required.check: GUARDIAN is never produced when the age is invalid (1e2, empty, 121) or the age is 18 or older (18 with null guardian is accepted).
required.rationale: Applying the guardian rule to an unparsed/default age 0 adds a fictitious GUARDIAN defect.

required.check: consent_txt passes only when `upperCase(trim(...))` equals "Y" ("y" and " Y " pass); N, null, blank and other text produce CONSENT, independently of age or guardian.
required.rationale: Comparing raw text rejects " Y "; inferring consent from a guardian accepts N.

required.check: visit_day_txt must have the exact whole-string yyyy-MM-dd shape: time-bearing "2026-04-01 00:00:00" and shortened "2026-4-1" fail VISIT (regex shape check, or strict isDate for short digits; trailing time text needs the explicit shape check). visit_day_txt is not trimmed: " 2026-04-01" fails VISIT.
required.rationale: A lenient or prefix parse accepts the time-bearing string the spec rejects.

required.check: A well-shaped visit day must be a real calendar date (strict check: 2026-02-30 fails) and lie between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30 inclusive (04-30 passes, 05-01 fails); the range test may compare typed dates or the validated yyyy-MM-dd strings lexicographically.
required.rationale: Exclusive bounds drop 04-30; lenient parsing accepts 02-30.

required.check: appointment_day is produced with the "UTC" time-zone argument (e.g. `str2date(d, "yyyy-MM-dd", "en.US", "UTC", true)`), giving midnight UTC; functions without a zone use the host zone (CET).
required.rationale: Host-zone parsing writes 2026-03-31 23:00 UTC for 2026-04-01.

required.check: program_txt is trimmed and upper-cased; WELL passes for any age (an invalid age adds no PROGRAM defect), SENIOR passes only with a valid age >= 65 (64 fails, 65 passes, invalid age fails), any other code fails PROGRAM.
required.rationale: Using the default age 0 or skipping the age-validity condition misjudges SENIOR.

required.check: Correction rows copy all source fields unchanged and set correction_codes to the defects in the order AGE, GUARDIAN, CONSENT, VISIT, PROGRAM joined by "," (no spaces, no trailing comma); accepted rows copy the source fields and add patient_age, appointment_day and normalized_program.
required.rationale: Wrong order or separators break the correction contract.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2integer on age_txt or str2date on visit_day_txt is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2integer("1e2") and strict str2date("2026-02-30") throw instead of producing AGE/VISIT.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP or ALL (or writes both $out.0 and $out.1 and returns ALL) for some rows, so a row is dropped or reaches both destinations.
forbidden.rationale: Every source row must reach exactly one destination; SKIP drops it and ALL duplicates it.

reference:
//#CTL2

Customs shipment and reversal validation

A bonded warehouse submits textual manifests to this Reformat before declaring goods. Output 0 posts signed customs values and output 1 retains evidence for the broker. Reversal requests can be incomplete independently of their numeric fields, and excessive digit counts must be rejected before conversion.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The customs gateway treats shipments and reversals as two different business movements. This Reformat sends valid manifests to output 0 and every invalid manifest to output 1. Each input is retained exactly once, including repeated manifest_id values.
2. Trim and uppercase movement_txt. SHIP and REVERSE are the only recognized movements. Null or blank fails MOVEMENT. This decision is independent of quantity, price and dispatch validity; unknown movement does not suppress their checks.
3. quantity_txt is trimmed and accepts an optional minus sign followed by one to six ASCII digits, with no plus sign, fractions or separators. Null and blank fail QTY. After a successful grammar check SHIP needs a positive quantity, REVERSE needs a negative quantity, and zero is always invalid; unknown movement imposes no sign rule.
4. unit_value_txt is a nonnegative decimal text with one to eight integer digits and optional one or two fractional digits. Trim it; null, empty, malformed and oversized text fail VALUE. Zero is valid for any recognized movement and must not be treated as missing.
5. A REVERSE movement additionally requires a trimmed nonempty original_manifest different from trimmed manifest_id. Null, blank or self-reference fails ORIGINAL. For other movement values the original reference is ignored, even if it is malformed or missing.
6. dispatch_txt accepts exactly yyyyMMdd, eight digits describing a real UTC calendar day. The text is not trimmed. Null, empty and surrounding whitespace fail DISPATCH, as do impossible dates or a timestamp suffix. A successful day is stored at midnight with no dependence on cargo_loaded.
7. Valid output adds signed_quantity, declared_value as signed quantity times unit value in decimal arithmetic, and dispatch_day. Every raw field is copied unchanged. Reversal values are negative; do not replace them with absolute values or apply a rounded floating point intermediate.
8. Rejected output copies the manifest with defect_list containing MOVEMENT, QTY, VALUE, ORIGINAL and DISPATCH in that sequence, separated by a vertical bar. No conversion occurs for a field whose grammar is invalid; retain per-port arrival order, null versus empty annotations and the first and last record.

rubric.description: Customs shipment and reversal validation

required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for valid manifests (written to $out.0) and 1 for invalid ones (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Any other return scheme loses or duplicates manifests.

required.check: movement_txt is trimmed and upper-cased; only SHIP and REVERSE are recognized, null/blank/other fail MOVEMENT, and an unrecognized movement does not suppress the QTY, VALUE and DISPATCH checks ("?" with null quantity yields MOVEMENT|QTY|VALUE|DISPATCH).
required.rationale: Returning early on an unknown movement hides the other defects.

required.check: quantity_txt grammar is a whole-string match on the trimmed text of an optional minus and 1–6 digits (e.g. `~= "-?[0-9]{1,6}"`): "+2", null and blank fail QTY, and str2integer is called only after the grammar passes.
required.rationale: Converting before the grammar check accepts +2 or throws on null.

required.check: After the grammar passes, SHIP requires a positive quantity and REVERSE a negative one (REVERSE 2 fails QTY); an unrecognized movement applies no sign rule.
required.rationale: Ignoring the movement-dependent sign accepts a positive reversal.

required.check: A zero quantity always fails QTY, including "-0" for REVERSE and 0 for SHIP (test the converted value, not the text).
required.rationale: A text test for a leading minus accepts -0 as a negative reversal.

required.check: unit_value_txt is validated as a whole-string match of 1–8 integer digits with optional 1–2 fraction digits, no sign (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,8}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`): "1e2" and empty fail VALUE, 99999999.99 passes, and 0 is valid (not treated as missing).
required.rationale: Conversion-based checks accept 1e2; a zero test treats 0 as missing.

required.check: For REVERSE, ORIGINAL is reported when trimmed original_manifest is null/blank or equals trimmed manifest_id (self-reference M0/M0 fails).
required.rationale: Checking only null misses the self-reference reversal.

required.check: For SHIP or an unrecognized movement, original_manifest is not checked at all (SHIP with "x" and "?" with "x" get no ORIGINAL).
required.rationale: Applying the reversal rule to every row adds spurious ORIGINAL defects.

required.check: dispatch_txt must be exactly 8 digits by an explicit whole-string shape check (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{8}"` or length 8 plus digits): "202611" and "20260101x" fail DISPATCH; strict date parsing alone is not verified to reject trailing text. dispatch_txt is not trimmed: " 20260101" fails DISPATCH.
required.rationale: Without a shape check a suffix after a valid day may be accepted.

required.check: A well-shaped dispatch_txt must be a real calendar day (strict isDate/str2date: 20260230 fails, 20240229 passes) and dispatch_day is parsed with the "UTC" time-zone argument so it is midnight UTC.
required.rationale: Lenient parsing accepts 20260230; host-zone parsing shifts the day by an hour.

required.check: declared_value is the signed quantity times the unit value as a decimal (e.g. `qty * str2decimal(v)`), negative for REVERSE (-2 × 1.25 = -2.50), and signed_quantity is the converted signed integer; raw source fields are copied unchanged.
required.rationale: Using abs() or the unsigned text loses the reversal sign.

required.check: Rejected rows copy all fields and set defect_list to the defects in the order MOVEMENT, QTY, VALUE, ORIGINAL, DISPATCH joined by "|" with no trailing separator.
required.rationale: Wrong order or separator breaks the broker evidence.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2integer/str2decimal/str2date is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2integer("+2"), str2decimal("1e2") or strict str2date("20260230") throw instead of producing a defect.

forbidden.check: declared_value is computed through number (double) arithmetic, e.g. decimal2double, a `number` variable or a floating intermediate that is then rounded.
forbidden.rationale: 99999899990000.01 is not representable exactly as a double; the spec requires exact decimal arithmetic.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP or ALL (or writes both $out.0 and $out.1 and returns ALL) for some rows, so a row is dropped or reaches both destinations.
forbidden.rationale: Every source row must reach exactly one destination; SKIP drops it and ALL duplicates it.

Policy migration with explicit override precedence

A policy administration replacement receives legacy records through this Reformat. Its output schema removes obsolete billing columns. The business must distinguish absence of an override from an intentionally blank override, while warnings continue to describe source defects even when suspension wins.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Migrate each policy to output 0 without dropping any row. Trim legacy_policy_no into policy_number; a trimmed empty identifier becomes UNASSIGNED. The identifier is never null, and duplicates or blank identifiers are source data rather than grouping keys.
2. Compute the normal billing mode after trimming and uppercase: M becomes MONTHLY, A becomes ANNUAL, and null, blank or unknown codes become MANUAL. An unknown nonblank source code contributes UNKNOWN_MODE to migration_warning even when another rule later overrides the effective mode.
3. manual_override is deliberately different from billing_mode: null means no override; trimmed empty means explicitly request MANUAL; normalized M or A chooses MONTHLY or ANNUAL. Any other nonblank override contributes BAD_OVERRIDE and leaves the previously computed source mode intact.
4. A true suspended flag has final precedence and forces mode_cd HOLD, regardless of either code. False or null means no suspension. Suspension must not erase source-code or override warnings; assemble UNKNOWN_MODE before BAD_OVERRIDE with a semicolon when both exist.
5. Normalize display_nm by trimming. Null or blank becomes Unnamed. Normalize email_txt by trimming and lowercase, preserving null as null and empty as empty. These missing policies differ; a name default must not cause an email default.
6. Copy credit_balance exactly, including negative and null amounts, and retired_at including null and any time portion. An epoch or midnight value is real data; no date truncation, currency rounding or replacement is requested.
7. All retained output fields are copied by name, including suspension, descriptive metadata and policy_unused. Remove old_policy_memo, old_billing_batch, old_agent_terminal, old_rate_table and old_conversion_tag completely. The legacy identifier, billing code and override have no destinations except their explicit computed mappings; every other retained source column survives unchanged. Never copy positions across different schemas or create undeclared columns.
8. Maintain input order and produce one output per source policy. Apply the precedence independently for every record, including a suspended first record, an invalid override after a valid override, and the final unsuspended record. Empty warnings are the empty string rather than null.

required.rationale: Copying the raw identifier keeps outer spaces; missing the default leaves an empty key.

required.check: billing_mode is trimmed and upper-cased null-safely: M → MONTHLY, A → ANNUAL, null/blank/unknown → MANUAL (" M " maps to MONTHLY).
required.rationale: Comparing the raw code maps " M " to MANUAL.

required.check: UNKNOWN_MODE is added only for a nonblank unrecognized billing code ("bad", "?"), not for null or blank billing_mode.
required.rationale: Treating null as unknown adds a spurious warning.

required.check: manual_override null and empty are distinguished: null means no override (source mode kept), while a non-null override that trims to empty forces MANUAL (" M " with override "" → MANUAL). `isBlank(override)` / `trim(nvl(override,"")) == ""` as the 'no override' test is wrong here.
required.rationale: Collapsing "" into null keeps MONTHLY where the spec demands MANUAL.

required.check: A trimmed, upper-cased override of M or A replaces the computed mode with MONTHLY or ANNUAL (unknown "?" source with override "m" → MONTHLY).
required.rationale: Ignoring a lowercase override keeps MANUAL.

required.check: Any other nonblank override adds BAD_OVERRIDE and leaves the source-computed mode unchanged (billing m, override "?" → MONTHLY with BAD_OVERRIDE).
required.rationale: Resetting the mode to MANUAL on a bad override discards the valid source mode.

required.rationale: Clearing warnings on HOLD or emitting null for none violates clauses 4 and 8.

required.rationale: Missing the null/blank default leaves null or " " names.

required.check: email_txt stays null when null; otherwise it is trimmed and lower-cased, so empty stays empty (" B@C " → "b@c"); it is never defaulted because the name was defaulted.

Property owner migration with ordered local deduplication

Land records from an older application contain all owners in one field. This Normalizer supplies a new ownership ledger with one record per retained owner. Missing ownership still needs a placeholder so the parcel cannot disappear during migration; all data arrives in its original order.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. This Normalizer migrates each legacy property into its owner rows on output 0. old_parcel_id is non-null and is trimmed into parcel_number, with UNKNOWN_PARCEL for trimmed empty. Do not combine source parcels merely because their identifiers repeat.
2. owners_txt represents owner names separated by semicolons. Trim every segment and discard empty segments, including leading, trailing and repeated delimiters. Null, empty or whitespace-only ownership text has no usable names; literal punctuation other than the delimiter is ordinary name content.
3. Within one property deduplicate usable owner names case-insensitively after trimming. Keep the spelling of the first appearance and preserve first-appearance order; the same owner in another source property remains a distinct emitted row.
4. When no usable owner exists emit exactly one placeholder with owner_name UNKNOWN_OWNER and owner_missing true. Otherwise emit every retained owner with owner_missing false. Neither null ownership nor a delimiter-only field may cause silent loss of its property.
5. owner_ordinal is one-based in the retained owner order and owner_total is the retained owner count. A placeholder uses ordinal 1 and total 1. Counts must be recomputed after blank removal and deduplication, not from the original separator count.
6. Translate normalized tenure_txt: F means FREEHOLD, L means LEASEHOLD, and null, empty or unknown means UNVERIFIED. Write tenure_code on every owner row; do not borrow a preceding property tenure when the current code is missing.
7. Carry the other retained property fields unchanged onto every child, including assessed_value with null or negative values, registered_at with time, street_label with null versus empty, property_unused and source row identity. Do not expose removed ownership text in the destination.
8. Finish all owners of one property before starting the next, preserving parcel input order. The first property can contain duplicate names and the last can be empty. Lists and duplicate tracking must start fresh per parent, including adjacent singleton properties.

Treasury entry migration with carried account balances

An obsolete treasury ledger stores opening and movement entries differently. This Reformat builds the destination balance history from a sorted stream. The graph guarantees account ordering but does not precompute balances; a row containing an invalid kind must remain visible without corrupting later entries.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Treasury entries arrive sorted by trimmed old_account, with stable source order inside each account. Upstream validation guarantees each non-null opening_balance and movement_amount has absolute value at most 1000000 and each account block has at most 1000 entries. Migrate every entry to output 0. Trim the non-null account identifier into account_key, retaining a blank key as a legitimate account rather than a missing account sentinel.
2. An account begins on the very first input or whenever its trimmed key differs from the previous entry. Reset its carried balance to zero and its ordinal to zero before processing that first entry. Epoch posting dates and empty account keys are legitimate values, not indications of uninitialized state.
3. Normalize entry_kind by trimming and uppercase. OPEN replaces the carried balance with opening_balance; null opening_balance means zero. OPEN ignores movement_amount entirely, including negative values. Multiple OPEN entries within one account intentionally replace earlier carried balances.
4. MOVE adds movement_amount to the current carried balance when the amount is non-null, including zero and negative amounts. A null movement_amount leaves the balance unchanged and reports MISSING_AMOUNT. Do not turn a null into an arithmetic operand.
5. CLOSE forces the carried balance to zero regardless of either numeric source field. It reports CLOSED and still emits an ordinary migrated entry. A later MOVE for that same account starts from this zero; no implicit new account is created.
6. Unknown, blank or null entry_kind leaves the carried balance unchanged and reports UNKNOWN_KIND. OPEN and valid MOVE report OK. These statuses describe only the current entry and must not carry forward after a prior defect.
7. Write the balance after applying the current entry to migrated_balance and assign account_entry_no starting at one for each account. Copy all original fields unchanged, including malformed kind text, nullable memo_text, posting_time with time and treasury_unused.
8. Preserve all duplicate source entries and account-local order. A singleton account gets one entry numbered one. Returning to a key would begin a new contiguous account block, although the supplied sorted stream prevents that case; the final account must be emitted completely.

rubric.description: Treasury entry migration with carried account balances

required.check: Single-output Reformat: transform() writes $out.0 and returns OK (or 0 / ALL) for every entry; the carried balance, ordinal and previous key live in global variables that persist between calls.
required.rationale: Local-only state cannot carry balances across records.

required.check: account_key = trim(old_account), and the account change test compares trimmed keys (" A " continues account A as entry 2).
required.rationale: Comparing raw keys starts a new account at " A ".

required.check: The first record is handled so that a blank key is a legitimate account: either an explicit first-record flag/counter, or a plain `k != previous` comparison relying on the declared defaults (previous "", balance 0, ordinal 0). A sentinel such as `previous == ""` / isBlank(previous) fails: the three leading blank-key rows must be numbered 1, 2, 3 with balance 2.00, 2.00, 0.00.
required.rationale: An empty-string sentinel resets the blank account on every row.

required.check: When the trimmed key differs from the previous entry, balance and ordinal are reset to zero before the current entry is applied (B after A starts at 0.00, entry 1).
required.rationale: Resetting after applying the entry or not at all carries A's balance into B.

required.check: entry_kind is trimmed and upper-cased null-safely; OPEN sets the balance to opening_balance, with null meaning zero (`nvl(opening_balance, 0D)`), ignores movement_amount, and a second OPEN replaces the earlier balance.
required.rationale: Adding instead of replacing, or a null opening, corrupts the balance.

required.check: MOVE with non-null movement_amount adds it to the balance, including zero and negative amounts, with status OK.
required.rationale: Skipping zero/negative amounts loses movements.

required.check: MOVE with null movement_amount leaves the balance unchanged and reports MISSING_AMOUNT, with no arithmetic on the null value.
required.rationale: balance + null throws or nulls the non-nullable balance.

required.check: CLOSE sets the balance to zero regardless of the numeric fields and reports CLOSED; the row is still emitted.
required.rationale: Keeping the balance or skipping the row breaks clause 5.

required.check: Unknown, blank or null entry_kind reports UNKNOWN_KIND and leaves the balance unchanged ("??" in A keeps 7.50).
required.rationale: Treating unknown kinds as zero resets loses the carried balance.

required.check: migration_status is decided fresh for every entry (e.g. a local status initialized to OK each call), so OK follows a MISSING_AMOUNT or UNKNOWN_KIND entry.
required.rationale: A global status carries a previous defect forward.

required.check: migrated_balance is the balance after the current entry, account_entry_no is the per-account ordinal starting at 1, and all original fields are copied unchanged (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*;` or per-field), including raw entry_kind.
required.rationale: Writing the pre-entry balance or a global row number misreports history.

forbidden.check: Resets account_entry_no (or treats the row as a new account) on CLOSE or OPEN instead of only on a key change.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 5 says a later MOVE continues the same account; only a key change starts one.

forbidden.check: Declares the carried balance or ordinal as a local variable inside transform() (reset on every record).
forbidden.rationale: Balances and ordinals then never carry from one entry to the next.

//#CTL2
boolean seen=false;string previous;decimal balance;integer ordinal;function integer transform(){string k=trim($in.0.old_account);if(!seen||k!=previous){balance=0D;ordinal=0;previous=k;seen=true;}string kind=upperCase(trim(nvl($in.0.entry_kind,"")));string status="OK";if(kind=="OPEN")balance=nvl($in.0.opening_balance,0D);else if(kind=="MOVE"){if($in.0.movement_amount==null)status="MISSING_AMOUNT";else balance+= $in.0.movement_amount;}else if(kind=="CLOSE"){balance=0D;status="CLOSED";}else status="UNKNOWN_KIND";ordinal++;$out.0.*=$in.0.*;$out.0.account_key=k;$out.0.migrated_balance=balance;$out.0.migration_status=status;$out.0.account_entry_no=ordinal;return OK;}
rubric_notes: First-record sentinel: plain `k != previous` with declared defaults is functionally correct here and accepted; `previous == null` is harmless dead code (never true) and not penalised; only an empty-string sentinel breaks the blank account.

A freight reader feeds this Reformat before scheduling. The in-memory ServiceRules table is supplied with metadata RouteRule and ordered key carrier_cd;service_cd. Expired exact matches are normal business data, so reference presence alone cannot determine whether the shipment has a usable commitment.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Enrich each freight shipment on output 0 using the graph simple lookup ServiceRules with composite key carrier_cd then service_cd. The reference loader guarantees unique key pairs. The table includes route-specific, carrier-wide and network-wide service commitments; all are real graph data rather than an inline codebook.
2. Trim and uppercase the two source keys solely for reference selection. Preserve their raw spelling in output. If either part is null or trimmed empty, make no reference queries and use the missing-reference result; both empty diagnostic parts still form a colon.
3. pickup_day is an exact typed timestamp, not a text value. Null pickup_day also disables all reference queries and produces the missing-reference result. Date-only midnight is ordinary data and participates in the same inclusive time comparisons as a timestamp.

Claim payout tariff selection over duplicate reference keys

Claims arrive unsorted at this Reformat. The graph supplies ClaimTariffs with ClaimTariff metadata and provider_id;region_id lookup key, allowing repeated reference keys. A new tariff can supersede an earlier tariff without deleting it, and the adjudicator needs a deterministic winner rather than whichever candidate the table returns first.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The claims Reformat enriches one output 0 row per incoming claim from ClaimTariffs, a simple graph lookup keyed by provider_id followed by region_id. Several reference rows may share a key; they are competing tariffs, not duplicate records to be ignored or combined.
2. Normalize both lookup keys with trim and uppercase while preserving their original values in output. Null or trimmed empty keys, or a null loss_at timestamp, prevent a query and produce the missing-tariff result. Repeated source keys must still yield independent claim decisions.
3. Read all reference candidates for a queryable key. A tariff is eligible only when loss_at falls in its inclusive effective_from to effective_to interval, with null effective_to meaning open-ended, and payout_percent is non-null and between 0 and 100 inclusive. Invalid percentages and future or expired candidates are ignored.
4. Choose among eligible tariffs by latest effective_from, then lowest admin_fee, then lexicographically smallest tariff_id. The fee is non-null; it is only a selection tie-break and is never deducted from payout. Lookup row order must not influence the winner.
5. For a winner set selected_tariff to its tariff_id and tariff_missing false. Compute payout from claim_amount multiplied by its percentage and divided by one hundred in exact decimal arithmetic, rounded half-up to two decimal places. A zero percentage is a valid winning tariff.
6. Null or negative claim_amount is payable as zero even when a tariff matches; retain the source value unchanged. A positive source amount follows the selected percentage. An amount of zero must remain zero and not trigger missing-tariff behavior.
7. When there is no eligible tariff, set selected_tariff to the empty string, tariff_missing true and payout to zero. A key hit with only ineligible candidates is a business miss. Never reuse a selected tariff or decimal payout from the preceding claim.
8. Preserve every input field, nullable notes, timestamps with time, unused claim data and source order. Emit the first and last claims as usual, including a miss after a zero-percent hit and two claims sharing the same keys but different loss timestamps.

Laboratory calibration with authoritative disable and fallback

An instrument export feeds this two-output Reformat before the clinical warehouse. FacilityFactors and AssayDefaults carry different reference metadata. Local disabling is a safety decision that overrides the general assay standard; a partially configured local factor, however, should use a valid general standard rather than block the measurement.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Enrich each laboratory result with an approved calibration. Output 0 receives calibrated samples and output 1 receives corrections. The graph supplies FacilityFactors keyed by facility_code then assay_code and AssayDefaults keyed by assay_code; both simple lookups have unique keys.
2. Trim and uppercase facility_txt. Null or trimmed empty contributes FACILITY and prevents reference selection. Other facility characters are accepted as identifiers. Preserve the source spelling and do not replace it with a reference field.
3. Trim and uppercase assay_txt. A valid assay has two to six ASCII characters, beginning with a letter and followed only by letters or digits. Null, empty and punctuation fail ASSAY. This grammar is independent of whether the reference tables contain a matching key.
4. Trim result_txt and accept an optional minus sign, one to six ASCII integer digits, and an optional decimal point with one to three fractional digits. Null, blank, plus signs, exponents and excess digits contribute VALUE. Zero and negative measurements are valid raw scientific results.
5. When any FACILITY, ASSAY or VALUE defect exists do not query either table. Reject with all those defects in that order, separated by semicolons. A malformed result must never be converted to build a reject row, even when the same row has a missing facility.
6. For syntactically valid input inspect the facility-specific record first. An explicit enabled false is an authoritative BLOCKED rejection with no fallback. Only enabled true and a non-null factor greater than zero and at most 1000000 provide a facility calibration; null enabled or a null, nonpositive or over-limit factor means try the assay default.
7. A missing facility record also tries the assay default. A non-null default factor greater than zero and at most 1000000 is usable; zero, negative, over-limit, null or a missing default contributes NO_FACTOR. A disabled facility must not be rescued by an otherwise valid assay default, and neither failed lookup may lend a stale value.
8. Accepted rows copy all source fields and add calibrated_result as raw decimal result multiplied by factor and rounded to two places with halves away from zero (2.505 to 2.51, -2.505 to -2.51), factor_used and factor_source FACILITY or DEFAULT. Rejected rows copy the original sample plus correction_reason; BLOCKED and NO_FACTOR are single reasons.
9. Keep every sample exactly once in its appropriate destination and preserve source order per port. Repeated sample identifiers are independent. Null versus empty lab_note and billing_amount survive, and the first success followed by failures must not leak its factor to the last sample.

Membership notices after semantic reconciliation

A loyalty operator wants useful change notifications rather than a byte-by-byte snapshot diff. Departure and arrival handlers already consume the one-sided streams; the CTL is confined to the middle reconciliation stream.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The DataIntersection receives yesterday on input 0 and today on input 1. Both are sorted by business_ref; join key is $business_ref=$business_ref. Equal NULL and Allow key duplicates are true. Ports 0 and 2 carry departures and arrivals unchanged; only a matched customer needs a notice decision.
2. For membership tier comparison alone, null, empty and whitespace mean the same absent tier; otherwise trim and uppercase. Keep the original tier text in the delivered record, including unrecognised codes.
3. Interpret interests_txt as semicolon-separated tokens. Discard blank tokens, trim and uppercase each remaining token, ignore repeated tokens, and compare the resulting sets without regard to their order. Null and empty are both the empty set; punctuation and text such as BAD:DATE are ordinary interest names.
4. Credit has changed if exactly one credit_limit is null, or when both are present and their absolute decimal difference is at least 0.05. Two nulls agree; a smaller difference is deliberately ignored. Do not round before this decision.
5. consent_until is compared as a complete nullable timestamp. Two nulls agree; null differs from every real date, and a midnight timestamp remains a real value. A time-only change within the same day matters.
6. Emit a NOTICE on the matched stream only when at least one semantic comparison changed. Its change_names lists TIER, INTERESTS, CREDIT, CONSENT in that order for the comparisons that changed, comma-separated without extra punctuation. A semantically unchanged pair produces no notice.
7. The notice carries every source field from today, even when a raw field differed but its normalised interpretation did not. Never replace the raw interest text with the canonical set or take yesterday's audit context.
8. Repeated keys produce their component-defined individual comparisons; no seen-key filter is allowed. Two old B rows and one new B row generate separate pairs. Decisions must not retain a prior pair's reason names. The first match and the final match follow the same rules as all intermediate pairs.

required.rationale: `upperCase(trim(null))` stays null while `""` stays empty, so the null-vs-empty pair (key A) falsely reports TIER.

required.rationale: Raw comparison reports TIER for whitespace/case-only differences that the spec says are equal.

required.check: interests_txt is split on ";" and every token is trimmed and upper-cased before comparison; punctuation inside a token (e.g. BAD:DATE) is kept as part of the name.
required.rationale: Comparing raw text makes `BAD:DATE` vs `bad:date` (key C) a spurious INTERESTS change.

required.check: Null interests_txt and blank tokens both give the empty set: null is guarded before `split` (or mapped to ""), and tokens that are empty after trimming are discarded, so null and " ; " compare equal.
required.rationale: Keeping blank tokens or splitting null makes the null vs " ; " pair (key A) report INTERESTS or fail.

Bank settlement gaps with absent partners

Treasury reconciles expected invoices against a bank extract. The join is deliberately full outer because both unexplained deposits and unpaid invoices matter; a bad amount belongs to repair rather than the settlement queue.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. An ExtMergeJoin uses FULL_OUTER joining on business_ref, ascending sorted inputs, with planned invoices on input 0 and bank entries on input 1. Both keys are non-null and unique per input. Only output 0 is connected to a reconciliation ledger. The ledger uses reconcile_kind REPAIR to send a row for data repair; other kinds identify settlement follow-ups.
2. Choose the audit context from the planned invoice whenever that side exists, including for a matched pair. A bank-only row instead takes its context from the bank record. An absent side has no usable key; a present side may contain nullable amounts and blank notes.
3. A bank record whose settlement_state is exactly VOID contributes decimal zero regardless of its settled_txt. In particular a VOID row with garbage text must not be parsed or rejected. Other spellings, null and empty state have no such exemption.
4. Otherwise settled_txt must be nonblank after trimming and match an optional minus sign followed by ASCII digits and an optional decimal part of one or two digits. Leading plus, exponents and commas are invalid. Accepted values have at most 10 integer digits and are parsed as decimals. A malformed present bank amount is retained as a REPAIR row with AMOUNT_TEXT.
5. A present invoice with null expected_amount is retained as a REPAIR row with EXPECTED_NULL unless malformed bank text already selected AMOUNT_TEXT. Negative planned or settled amounts are legitimate corrections. On repair rows settled_amount and remaining_amount are null even if some other quantity was usable; expected_amount is the invoice's value as read, or zero when there is no invoice.
6. For valid comparisons, a missing invoice means expected_amount zero, and a missing bank entry means settled_amount zero. Compute remaining_amount as expected minus settled using exact decimals. Always retain those three computed quantities on a follow-up row.
7. A valid matched pair with remaining_amount zero is omitted. All one-sided rows are retained even if their amount is zero. Label an invoice-only row WAITING and a bank-only row UNPLANNED; for a matched nonzero remainder use SHORT when positive and EXCESS when negative.
8. For a repair row use reconcile_kind REPAIR and the selected error_reason. For a follow-up row error_reason is empty. Write every context field, keep null distinct from empty and preserve the merger's order in the reconciliation ledger. A date-only midnight and unparsed date-looking notes are ordinary context.
9. The first invoice-only, a first bank-only, zero corrections, and the final matched pair all use the same side-presence and precedence rules. Never substitute a numeric default for a present null invoice or emit two different dispositions for one pair.

required.check: ExtMergeJoin FULL_OUTER contract: one `transform()` is called for every matched pair and for every one-sided record (the absent side's fields are null), writes `$out.0` and returns OK/0/ALL to emit or SKIP to omit.
required.rationale: Assuming one-sided records bypass the transform (or need separate callbacks) loses WAITING/UNPLANNED rows.

required.check: Side presence is detected from something that is null only for an absent side: the non-nullable `business_ref` of that side (`isnull($in.0.business_ref)`), or record-level `isnull($in.N)` / `$in.N == null`; never from a nullable amount or text field.
required.rationale: Testing `isnull($in.0.expected_amount)` turns the present invoice G (null amount) into a bank-only UNPLANNED row instead of EXPECTED_NULL.

required.check: Context comes from the invoice (`$in.0`) whenever it is present, including matched pairs, and from the bank (`$in.1`) only when the invoice is absent (e.g. `$out.0.* = $in.0.*` in one branch, `$out.0.* = $in.1.*` in the other), copying every context field verbatim.

required.check: A present bank row whose settlement_state is exactly "VOID" (case-sensitive `==`, no trim) gets settled amount 0 and its settled_txt is neither validated nor parsed.

required.check: For non-VOID bank rows, the trimmed settled_txt must fully match an optional minus, 1–10 ASCII digits and an optional '.' with 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "-?[0-9]{1,10}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`) before `str2decimal`; plus sign, exponent (1e2), commas and longer fractions fail.

required.check: AMOUNT_TEXT takes precedence over EXPECTED_NULL when a pair has both a malformed bank amount and a null invoice amount.

Supplier master winner selection

The master loader needs one actual supplier version per key, including low-quality records for remediation. Timestamp order inside a group is unspecified; an upstream Sort supplies key ordering only.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Supplier versions arrive sorted only by supplier_ref_no; every key must yield one real winning source row. A complete version has non-null, trimmed nonblank legal_nm, tax_country and payment_iban. Trimming classifies quality but does not edit the winner.
2. Complete versions outrank incomplete ones, regardless of recency. Within an equal quality rank, a real revision_at outranks null, even before the Unix epoch; later complete timestamps win. A date-only value is midnight and is never treated as missing.
3. When timestamps agree, including null against null, greater revision_no wins. An exact tie retains the earlier arriving row; revision numbers are non-null and duplicate values are legitimate.
4. Copy every field of the selected source version, including estimated_value, nullable context and the original whitespace in completeness fields. Do not construct a new version by combining fields from several candidates.
5. Count all candidates as versions_seen, including repeated versions. Set winner_complete from the selected record's quality; even an incomplete singleton is emitted with count one.
6. The first version of each key must become the candidate before comparing rank. Neither a default date nor a default revision number denotes a missing first record.
7. Groups are independent: winner eligibility, rank and count must not survive into the next key. Consecutive incomplete-only and null-timestamp-only groups still emit correctly; the final group is not forgotten.
8. Empty string and null both fail completeness while retaining their original representation in output. Text such as BAD:DATE in tax_country is still nonblank for this task; completeness is not semantic field validation. Do not parse completeness fields as dates or amounts.

Receipt decisions before the final chosen receipt

A point-of-sale repair pipeline requires an audit decision for every arriving receipt and a separate final winner stream. The Rollup owns both decisions: a duplicate can be rejected immediately, while the eventual chosen receipt must keep its own original context.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. A receipt-control Rollup is grouped on business_ref after sorting only on that field. It has output 0 for one disposition per input receipt and output 1 for one final chosen receipt per group, provided the group has a candidate. Receipt order within a group is arrival order.
2. A usable identifier is non-null and nonblank after trimming. Use trimming only to test blankness; identifiers compare in their raw spelling, so R and space-R-space are distinct. Empty, null and whitespace-only identifiers get INVALID and never enter the duplicate register.
3. For a usable identifier the first arriving occurrence reserves that identifier, even when voided or amount is null/nonpositive. Later occurrences of that exact identifier get DUPLICATE before any amount or void checks and cannot become a winner.
4. A first occurrence is a candidate only when voided is false and amount is non-null and strictly positive. The earliest such candidate becomes the group winner; later candidates get ELIGIBLE but do not replace it. First occurrences that fail candidate quality get INELIGIBLE; the chosen occurrence gets WINNER.
5. Each output-0 record copies that input receipt unchanged, adds its disposition, and sets winner_receipt to the winner identifier known after considering that receipt, or null if none is known. rows_seen is the inclusive arrival count within its group.
6. At group completion output 1 copies the entire chosen receipt unchanged, uses disposition CHOSEN, winner_receipt equal to its own raw identifier, and rows_seen equal to the final group size. No winner means no output-1 record; the per-receipt dispositions must still be delivered.
7. Never send interim winner records to output 1. The two output streams have separate meanings and must not receive the same annotated record merely because both writers are connected. Duplicate inputs count separately in every arrival count.
8. Clear identifier membership and winner state between groups. A singleton with positive amount wins; an all-invalid or all-ineligible group has no chosen row. Preserve null amounts and unused archive context, and handle the first and final groups without losing their dispositions.
9. Identifier strings are not parsed: BAD:DATE is a valid nonblank identifier. A date at midnight is copied as supplied; an empty note remains empty while a null note stays null. The chosen row's context may differ from both the first and final group row.

Inventory survivor evidence after retractions

Warehouse messages can retract an earlier candidate and then add it again. A single running best value cannot answer the final request because the previous best may disappear. The downstream warehouse audit needs both the winner and the complete surviving evidence.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The inventory Denormalizer groups by business_ref on a stream sorted by that field only. Produce one survivor summary for every warehouse key in group order, including an empty survivor group. The context fields come from the first source record.
2. A usable slot_id is non-null and nonblank after trimming, but comparisons and evidence retain its raw spelling. Ignore operations on unusable identifiers while still counting their rows. Unknown operations, including null and differently cased spelling, are ignored.
3. An operation exactly REMOVE retracts every earlier retained ADD with that raw slot_id. A REMOVE never prevents a later ADD of the same slot. Removing an unknown slot is harmless. Remaining evidence keeps the arrival order of surviving additions, including repeated additions.
4. An operation exactly ADD is retained only when units_txt, after trimming, matches ASCII digits with an optional decimal part of one or two digits, at most nine integer digits, and the parsed value is strictly positive. Signs, exponent, blank, null and malformed text are ignored without a parsing failure; other rows in that key still survive.
5. Choose among surviving additions by greatest chosen_units first. If units tie, prefer a non-null observed_at over null, then the latest complete timestamp. A remaining tie retains the earlier addition. Dates before the epoch and date-only midnight are legitimate times.
6. The summary chosen_slot, chosen_at, chosen_units and chosen_cost all come from the same chosen addition; chosen_cost may be null or negative and does not affect ranking. A warehouse with no survivors sets those four fields to null.
7. surviving_slots is the raw slot identifiers of retained additions in their current arrival order, joined with a comma. There is no trailing comma, and no survivors means an empty string. It is evidence of every survivor, not just the selected winner.
8. rows_seen counts every input including ignored malformed additions and repeated removals. Copy every remaining context field from the saved first record, including its nullable context_value and unused_archive_label; do not use the last addition's context.
9. Each new warehouse starts with empty retained history and fresh count. Do not let a prior removal or candidate influence the next group. The first warehouse, an empty middle warehouse, a final singleton and duplicate slot identifiers must all satisfy the same rules.

required.check: Denormalizer contract: `append()` processes every record of the warehouse group into list state; `transform()` runs once per group and writes one summary to `$out.0`, including for a group with no survivors.
required.rationale: Emitting only when a winner exists drops the empty warehouse B.

required.check: Context fields are saved from the first record of the group (flag or count == 0) and written from that saved copy, including nullable context_value and unused_archive_label; not from `$in.0` in transform() (the last record).
required.rationale: Copying `$in.0` in transform() writes source_row 7 instead of 1 for warehouse A.

required.check: rows_seen counts every input record, incremented before any early return for ignored rows (bad slot, unknown op, malformed units, repeated removes).
required.rationale: Counting after the guards reports 6 instead of 7 for warehouse A.

required.check: A row is ignored for state (but still counted) when slot_id is null or blank after trim, or when operation is not exactly "ADD" or "REMOVE" (case-sensitive, null-safe `==`); usable slot ids keep their raw spelling in comparisons and evidence.
required.rationale: Upper-casing operations or trimming ids changes which rows count as ADD/REMOVE.

required.check: REMOVE deletes every earlier retained addition with the same raw slot_id from all parallel lists (iterating backwards, or rebuilding the lists), not just the first or last match.
required.rationale: Removing a single match leaves one of S's two additions alive in warehouse A.

required.check: A REMOVE does not block later ADDs of that slot (no permanent tombstone set); removing an unknown slot is a no-op.
required.rationale: A tombstone set drops the re-added S 3.50 that must appear in the evidence.

required.check: An ADD is retained only if the trimmed units_txt fully matches 1–9 digits with an optional '.' and 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,9}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`) checked before `str2decimal`, and the parsed value is > 0; null, blank, signs, exponent and malformed text are ignored without throwing.

required.rationale: Picking the last or first survivor ignores units ranking.

required.check: Among equal units, a non-null observed_at beats null, and between two non-null values the later full date-time wins (pre-epoch and midnight are real times).
required.rationale: Warehouse A's three survivors all have 3.50 units, so only these timestamp rules select T at 2026-01-01 over S (1960) and T (null).

Account dimension versioning

A history resolver attaches prior account values to each event before this Reformat. Two database writers accept closing updates and inserted versions. DimKeys is a long sequence owned by the graph, starting at 900000 and incrementing by one.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. A resolved account event arrives with optional prior current version values. previous_sk null means a new account; otherwise previous_from is non-null. Compare the incoming risk_class and contract_value with previous_risk_class and previous_value. row_kind is merely a label, never a route.
2. An existing version is unchanged only if both tracked attributes agree under null-safe equality. Null agrees with null but differs from empty text or numeric zero. Unchanged existing events emit no records and consume no surrogate key.
3. A changed existing account closes on output 0: version_sk is previous_sk, valid_from is previous_from, valid_to is event_at, and is_current is false. The closing risk_class and contract_value must be the prior attribute values, not the incoming replacements.
4. Every new account and changed account opens on output 1 with incoming attributes, valid_from event_at, null valid_to and is_current true. Obtain its long surrogate from the graph-managed DimKeys sequence, initially 900000 with step one.
5. Consume precisely one DimKeys value per opening version. A closing record, an unchanged record and any inspection of input placeholders must not allocate another key; never reset the sequence in CTL.
6. Dates are prevalidated UTC. An event with a prior version is strictly later than previous_from. Windows are half-open: the old valid_to equals the new valid_from exactly. Midnight is valid; do not create a second/day gap.
7. Changed existing accounts require both writers, while a new account requires only the insert writer. Repeated account keys are allowed because the resolver supplies the right prior version separately for each event; the component must keep arrival order without its own reconciliation buffer.
8. Copy every other common source field to each emitted record. Overwrite incoming version_sk, valid_from, valid_to and is_current placeholders in all cases. Preserve nullable audit context, unused_archive_label, date values and original spellings.
9. The first event may be a new account whose attributes are both null: it still opens. The final event may be a null-to-empty change: it still closes and opens. required.rationale: Testing previous_risk_class/previous_value for null misclassifies existing accounts with null prior attributes (D, F).

required.check: 'Changed' compares risk_class with previous_risk_class and contract_value with previous_value using null-safe `!=` (or explicit null handling), without nvl/trim normalisation, so null vs "" and null vs 0.00 are changes and null vs null is not.
required.rationale: nvl/isBlank normalisation hides the null→"" (F) and null→0.00 (D row 6) changes.

required.check: A new account always opens, even when both incoming attributes are null (the existence test comes before or overrides the unchanged test).
required.rationale: Comparing two nulls first makes the all-null new account A row 1 look unchanged and drops it.

required.check: An unchanged existing account returns SKIP before any `sequence(...).next()` call.

1. This Normalizer receives pre-resolved tariff requests; its sole output 0 feeds an operation ledger that distinguishes version operations from audit records using record_kind. A request_kind of CANCEL withdraws a current tariff; every other spelling requests the incoming tariff. previous_sk null means there is no current version.
2. For a tariff request, null or trimmed empty new_rate_txt means an unpriced tariff with rate null. Otherwise accept only ASCII digits, at most eight integer digits, optionally followed by one or two decimal digits. Signs, exponent, commas and malformed text produce one audit ERROR with audit_note BAD_RATE and no version records.
3. CANCEL takes precedence over rate validation. Ignore new_rate_txt completely on cancellation, even if malformed. If a previous version exists, close it; cancellation always creates an audit CANCELLED record, regardless of audit_requested, and never consumes a sequence value.
4. An existing requested tariff whose parsed rate equals previous_rate under null-safe equality does not create versions. If audit_requested is true it creates one audit UNCHANGED record; otherwise it is silent. A new tariff opens even if its rate is null.
5. A replacement emits two version records in order: CLOSE of the prior version followed by OPEN of the new one. A new tariff emits only OPEN. A cancellation emits only CLOSE when applicable. All expansions go to output 0; record_kind supplies the version or audit operation.
6. CLOSE uses the previous surrogate, previous_from and previous_rate, with valid_to event_at and is_current false. OPEN gets one long value from graph sequence PriceKeys (starts 1000, step one), valid_from event_at, valid_to null and is_current true. UTC dates are prevalidated and every existing-version event is after previous_from; boundaries are half-open with no time subtraction.
7. For a changed or new tariff with audit_requested true, append an audit REPRICED record after its version records. It carries the new version fields. CANCELLED and UNCHANGED audit records carry the previous version fields, with valid_to event_at for CANCELLED and null for UNCHANGED. is_current is false on CANCELLED and true on UNCHANGED. A missing previous version gives null version fields, including is_current, on CANCELLED; ERROR likewise has all version fields null.
8. Every emitted row copies all base context from that request, including unused_archive_label and nullable context_value. audit_note is empty except for BAD_RATE. Audit rows carry their specified audit record_kind in the same ledger; never obtain another key merely for the audit copy.
9. Preparation is independent per request. Preserve order among expansions of one request and among requests in the ledger. A malformed middle request, a silent unchanged request, a new null-rate first request and a cancellation at the final request must not reuse an earlier prepared count, key or rate.

required.check: Normalizer contract: `count()` returns the number of ledger rows for the request (0 for a silent unchanged request) and `transform(integer idx)` builds row idx on the single output `$out.0`.
required.rationale: A fixed count or SKIP-based filtering emits wrong numbers of rows per request.

required.check: request_kind == "CANCEL" (exact) is tested before any rate validation, and new_rate_txt is ignored on cancellation (no regex test or str2decimal on it).
required.rationale: Validating first turns cancellation D ('BAD:DATE') into an ERROR row.

required.check: A cancellation with previous_sk emits CLOSE then CANCELLED (CANCELLED carrying previous_sk, previous_from, valid_to = event_at and previous_rate); without previous_sk it emits only CANCELLED with null version_sk, valid_from, valid_to and rate; it is emitted regardless of audit_requested and allocates no PriceKeys value. (is_current on CANCELLED is not graded.)
required.rationale: Gating CANCELLED on audit_requested drops the always-required audit row for D, E and I.

required.check: For a non-cancel request, null or blank (after trim) new_rate_txt means an unpriced tariff with rate null — not an error.
required.rationale: Treating blank as malformed turns request F into ERROR instead of UNCHANGED.

required.check: Non-blank rate text must fully match 1–8 digits with an optional '.' and 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,8}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"` on the trimmed text) before `str2decimal`; signs, exponent (1e2) and commas fail.
required.rationale: `str2decimal("1e2")` may succeed, so parsing first accepts request G instead of rejecting it.

required.check: A malformed rate produces exactly one row (count 1): record_kind ERROR, audit_note BAD_RATE, version_sk/valid_from/valid_to/rate null, with no version rows and no key allocation.
required.rationale: Emitting versions or a second row for a bad rate breaks the ledger contract.

required.check: An existing tariff is unchanged when the parsed rate equals previous_rate under null-safe equality (null == null unchanged; 0 vs null changed).
required.rationale: A non-null-safe compare makes F (null vs null) a change and H ('0' vs null) unchanged.

required.check: An unchanged tariff emits nothing (count 0) when audit_requested is false, and one UNCHANGED row when true, carrying previous_sk, previous_from, previous_rate and valid_to null. UNCHANGED has is_current true.
required.rationale: Always emitting UNCHANGED creates audit rows nobody asked for (request B).

required.check: A replacement emits CLOSE first — version_sk previous_sk, valid_from previous_from, valid_to event_at (no subtraction), is_current false, rate previous_rate — then OPEN; a new tariff (no previous_sk) emits only OPEN, even with a null rate.
required.rationale: Reversed order or a CLOSE for a new tariff corrupts the version ledger.

required.check: OPEN takes exactly one PriceKeys value — `sequence(PriceKeys,long).next()` once per opening, in `count()` (saved to a variable) or in `transform()` at the OPEN index — with valid_from event_at, valid_to null, is_current true and the parsed rate.
required.rationale: Calling next() per row or per transform call skips keys (expected 1000, 1001, 1002).

required.check: When audit_requested is true for a new or changed tariff, a REPRICED row follows the version rows and carries the same new version fields, reusing the OPEN key (saved variable or `sequence(PriceKeys,long).current()`).
required.rationale: A fresh next() for the audit copy gives REPRICED a key different from its OPEN.

required.check: Per-request preparation state (flags, parsed rate, new key, count) is recomputed or reset at the start of each `count()` (or in `clean()`), so a malformed or silent request does not reuse the previous request's rate or key.
required.rationale: A stale parsed rate or new key from request C would leak into later rows.

forbidden.check: Allocates a PriceKeys value for a cancellation, an ERROR, an unchanged request or a CLOSE row.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 3/8 forbid it, and it shifts every subsequent key.

forbidden.check: Returns STOP or calls `raiseError` for a malformed rate instead of emitting the ERROR row.
forbidden.rationale: The spec requires a defined ERROR/BAD_RATE ledger row, not an aborted graph.

Service-region history carried through consecutive events

The geographic service feed provides a seed only when entering a new reference run. Several later events for that reference may change the state again. This Reformat maintains the accepted state and uses GeoKeys, a graph-managed long sequence starting at 3000 and stepping by one.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. This Reformat receives contiguous runs of business_ref in ascending key order and effective_at order. Output 0 updates closing versions and output 1 inserts openings. The empty reference string is a legitimate key; it must not be mistaken for uninitialised state.
2. Only the first row of a key may use seed_sk, seed_from, seed_region and seed_fee. A non-null seed_sk introduces a current historical version; seed_from is then non-null. Subsequent seed fields can be stale and must be ignored: compare against the current state accepted by this component.
3. The tracked state is the exact nullable region_cd and service_fee pair. Null equals null, empty region differs from null, and numeric zero differs from null. An unchanged row emits nothing, does not advance GeoKeys, and does not replace the saved current context or starting date.
4. If no current version exists, open the incoming state even when both attributes are null. Every opening receives one long graph-managed GeoKeys value, initially 3000 with step one, valid_from effective_at, null valid_to and is_current true.
5. For a changed existing state, first build a closing record on output 0 using its current surrogate, saved starting date and saved tracked attributes, valid_to equal to the incoming effective_at and is_current false. Send the opening on output 1. Exactly one sequence value is used for this pair.
6. Closing context for a seeded version comes from the first row that introduced that seed. Closing context for a component-created version comes from the row that opened it. Openings always use the current input context. Preserve every context field including notes and unused_archive_label.
7. When an opening succeeds, remember its full context, attributes, assigned key and starting date for later events. A later unchanged row must not erase that stored source. Reset the whole current-state interpretation when business_ref changes, even following a silent first row.
8. All dates are prevalidated UTC. Changed events are strictly later than the accepted current start; duplicate unchanged events may have the same time. Half-open windows meet at exactly effective_at, including midnight. Date-looking notes such as 2025-02-30 remain unparsed text.
9. Keep arrival order within each destination, emitting new keys only to port 1 and changes to both ports. Handle the first empty-string key, exact duplicate events, null-to-empty attribute transitions, singleton keys, and the final seeded key without dropping or broadcasting records.

required.check: A new key is detected by comparing business_ref with the saved previous key using explicit presence — a boolean flag, a row counter, or a key variable explicitly initialised to null (`string prev = null;`, valid because business_ref is non-nullable) — so a first key "" is still seen as new.
required.rationale: A bare `string prev;` starts as "" and equals the empty first key, so its seed/state initialisation is skipped.

required.check: Seed fields are read only on the first row of a key: a non-null seed_sk sets the current version to (seed_sk, seed_from, seed_region, seed_fee); a null seed_sk means no current version.
required.rationale: Ignoring the seed on key A's first row opens a new version instead of recognising E/5.00 as unchanged.

required.check: On later rows of the same key the seed fields are ignored and comparisons use the state accepted by the component.
required.rationale: Comparing with the stale seed (999/STALE/9.00 on row 2) produces a spurious change.

required.check: The change test compares region_cd and service_fee with the saved current values using null-safe `!=` (or explicit null handling): null == null, "" ≠ null and 0 ≠ null.
required.rationale: nvl-style normalisation hides the null→"" change on row 3.

required.rationale: Updating the saved context on silent row 2 makes the later close carry r2 instead of r1.
