user_message:
Claim monthly report with override and reopening controls

The claims reporting writer still needs the monthly business buckets and first-event context. New correction feeds supply a textual override and late waivers, while operations also wants to know whether a paid claim was immediately reopened. These decisions belong in this one Rollup.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Claims arrive at a Rollup sorted and grouped by group_key, a key that already combines tenant, claim unit and UTC calendar month. Every group is nonempty and requires one monthly summary on output 0. Typed dates follow a UTC business calendar; the runtime default timezone may differ.
2. period_label is yyyy-MM using the group month. Preserve every base context field from the first claim event, including claim_ref_no, source_row_no and operator_note, which may vary later in the group. The unused_archive_label is still part of that saved context.
3. An amount_override_txt that is null means use net_amount, including its possible null. A non-null override must trim to a complete ASCII decimal with an optional minus sign, one to ten integer digits, and an optional decimal point followed by one or two fractional digits; leading plus is invalid; null is the only fallback trigger. Empty, whitespace, exponent, impossible-date text and malformed overrides increment bad_amount_rows and contribute no amount, even if net_amount was usable.
4. rows_seen counts all events. For usable effective amounts, paid_total sums status_cd exactly PAID and pending_total sums exactly PENDING. Unknown, null, empty and differently cased statuses contribute to neither bucket. Negative amounts reduce their bucket; a missing amount contributes nothing.
5. billable_average uses usable non-null effective amounts on billable true events only. Its divisor counts these amounts, including zero and negative ones, independently of their payment status. Round the decimal mean half-up to two places; no eligible amounts means null rather than zero.
6. A late event has non-null delay_days greater than two and late_waived false. A waived event is not late even when the delay is large. late_percent is 100 times the late count divided by every rows_seen, decimal division rounded half-up to two places. A bad amount still participates in delay classification and the denominator.
7. reopened_rows counts adjacent arrivals where the immediately preceding status was exactly PAID and the current status is exactly PENDING. Amount validity, billability and waiver do not affect this transition count. The first event of each group has no predecessor; null/empty status does not mean PAID.
8. Accumulate each event exactly once and emit a summary only at group end. Reset counts, sums, predecessor presence/status and saved first context between groups. All-null amount groups still have row counts and percentages, and must not inherit a predecessor from the previous group.
9. Conserve repeated inputs as separate arrivals. Handle a singleton group, a 1-in-3 late fraction, an invalid override in the middle, a first and final group, and a date without time. Copy null and empty context verbatim rather than parsing date-looking notes or silently discarding a failed amount event.

2. For the summary copy every base context field from the first valuation, preserving null and empty notes and unused_archive_label. audit_required from that first valuation determines whether an empty eligible population is auditable; later audit_required values cannot change that decision.

Basket rows retain optional nested notes

A checkout ingestion graph supplies validated JSON baskets to one Normalizer. The next writer stores children keyed by source-row identity and ordinal. Parent monetary and calendar fields have already been typed by the reader; unknown JSON properties are harmless. The component must retain the business context without interpreting optional absence as a reused value.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Flatten the basket JSON into child-table rows. A nonblank payload has an object root whose lines member is either missing, null or an array; null, empty and whitespace-only payloads, missing lines, null lines and an empty array each produce no children.
2. Array elements are objects with a required nonblank sku string. Preserve its exact spelling, internal and surrounding whitespace as child_code; repeated codes remain separate children. Parent references may repeat and must never be used as a cache key.
3. Assign ordinal from the original one-based array position, beginning with 1 and ending at the array length. Parents arrive in source order and all children of one parent precede the next parent’s children; no sorting or duplicate removal is permitted.
4. An optional details member is missing, null or an object. Its optional note is missing, null or a string. Missing/null details or note yields child_note null; an explicitly empty note stays empty, and every other note retains whitespace unchanged.

7. Per-parent extraction state must be replaced before examining the next payload. A populated basket followed by a missing-array basket emits nothing for the latter, even if their basket_key values are identical.
8. Each valid array position emits exactly one output. Parent context belongs to its own source row, including the first and last inputs, empty notes and the archive field. Equipment channels are ordered by map key

A factory receives telemetry objects with dynamically named channels rather than a fixed sensor array. The Normalizer fans each envelope into an observation relation consumed by maintenance analytics. The schema validator guarantees object shapes and property types, but device firmware may still send bad numeric text. Disabled channels are intentionally opaque and should never trigger parsing failures.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The equipment payload is either null/blank or a JSON object with optional channels, itself missing, null or an object keyed by channel names. Empty envelopes and absent/null/empty channel maps produce zero observations. Each channel value is a non-null object and its key is a nonempty ASCII string.
2. Visit keys in ascending case-sensitive lexical order, independently of JSON property insertion order. position is the one-based position in this sorted list of all channel keys. A suppressed channel still occupies its position, so emitted positions may have gaps.
3. A channel has optional enabled, which is boolean or null. Only an explicit false suppresses the channel; missing and null enabled mean enabled. Suppressed entries may contain arbitrary malformed value text and must be discarded before reading or parsing that text.
4. For enabled entries the optional value is null, missing or a string. Missing/null/trimmed-empty becomes reading_value null and quality_cd MISSING. Distinguish genuine zero from missing and preserve a signed valid decimal exactly at two output places.
5. A nonblank value is valid only when its trimmed text matches an optional minus, one through six digits, and optionally a dot followed by one or two digits. Otherwise still emit the observation with null reading_value and quality_cd BAD_TEXT. Valid numeric text produces quality_cd GOOD; no conversion error may abort this graph.
6. The exact channel name is copied, without uppercasing. Metadata context including rated_capacity, commissioned_on, machine_note and machine_unused_archive accompanies each enabled entry; omit only channels_json from the child record.
7. Each equipment envelope starts with a new map and key list. Repeated machine_key values refer to separate measurements. A missing map after a populated map must produce no stale observations; a singleton map emits position 1 even on the final parent.
8. The output follows parent arrival order, then sorted channel-key order, retaining repeated equipment and repeated values.

required.check: Normalizer contract: `count()` returns the number of channel keys of the current envelope (or the number of enabled ones when suppression is done there) and `transform(integer idx)` builds the observation for sorted key `idx`.
required.rationale: A count unrelated to the key list emits too few or too many observations.

required.check: A null or blank `channels_json`, or a missing or null `channels` member, makes `count()` return 0 (missing key: `containsKey(...)` or a null test on the value; blank: `isBlank`, `trim(nvl(x,"")) == ""` or equivalent).
required.rationale: `getKeys` on a null channels value fails instead of producing zero observations.

required.check: The key list (and channel map) is rebuilt for every envelope: cleared/replaced at the start of `count()`, in `clean()`, or held in fresh locals, so keys of a previous envelope never accumulate.
required.rationale: Appending to a global list without clearing re-emits the previous machine's channels for a later envelope with a missing map.

required.check: Channel names are obtained with `getKeys(...)` and ordered with `sort(...)` on the exact strings (no `lowerCase`/`upperCase` in the comparison); `sort()` on strings is case-sensitive by UTF-16 code unit, so `Z` precedes `a`.
required.rationale: Using JSON insertion order or a case-folded sort produces the wrong sequence and positions.

required.check: `position` is the one-based index in the sorted list of ALL keys, so a suppressed channel keeps its number and leaves a gap: either `transform(idx)` returns SKIP for a suppressed channel with `position = idx + 1`, or `count()` filters suppressed channels while keeping each emitted channel's original sorted position number.
required.rationale: Renumbering after suppression shifts every later position by one.

required.check: Only an explicit `enabled == false` suppresses; a missing or null `enabled` means enabled (the code tests presence/null before casting to boolean).
required.rationale: Casting a missing or null enabled to boolean either fails or treats the channel as disabled.

required.check: The enabled test happens before the code reads, trims, regex-checks or parses the channel's `value`.
required.rationale: Parsing first lets arbitrary malformed text in a disabled channel trigger a failure or a BAD_TEXT row.

required.check: For an enabled channel whose `value` is missing, null or empty after trim, the output has `reading_value` null and `quality_cd` MISSING.
required.rationale: Defaulting missing to 0 conflates it with a genuine zero reading.

required.check: The trimmed value is checked against the full grammar optional minus, 1–6 integer digits, optionally a dot and 1–2 fractional digits (e.g. regex `-?[0-9]{1,6}(\.[0-9]{1,2})?`) before conversion; `str2decimal` alone is not enough because it accepts out-of-grammar text such as `1.234` or `1234567`.
required.rationale: Without the explicit check, over-precise or over-long readings are reported GOOD.

required.check: A nonblank value that fails the grammar still emits the observation with `reading_value` null and `quality_cd` BAD_TEXT, and no conversion is attempted on it (so nothing throws).
required.rationale: Calling str2decimal on unchecked text aborts the graph on firmware garbage.

required.check: A value that passes the grammar gets `quality_cd` GOOD and `reading_value` = `str2decimal` of the trimmed text (decimal conversion, keeping sign and zero).
required.rationale: Converting through double or treating 0 as absent alters an exact valid reading.

required.check: `channel_name` is the map key exactly as read (no case change or trim), and parent fields come from the current input record (e.g. `$out.0.* = $in.0.*`).
required.rationale: Uppercasing the key changes the channel identity analytics joins on.

forbidden.check: Obtains channel names by `foreach` over the channels map/variant (which yields values, not keys) instead of `getKeys(...)`.
forbidden.rationale: Map foreach yields the channel objects, so names and sort order are wrong.

forbidden.check: Detects the first envelope (or a new envelope) by testing an uninitialized global string/date for null.
forbidden.rationale: Declared strings start as "" and dates at epoch, never null, so the test never fires (clause 8 names this trap).

user_message:
Overdue payment routing bypasses irrelevant amount defects

A payment operations graph uses this Partition to feed terminal, held, overdue, review, routine and defect queues. A separate Reformat on the defect branch derives the reason; all Partition edges retain the full source record. Credit controllers care about old invoices before value-based review, so a defect in a lower-priority attribute must not displace a business decision already made.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Six connected payment queues share the input metadata: 0 terminal, 1 manual hold, 2 overdue, 3 high value, 4 ordinary, and 5 defective text. Each row reaches exactly one queue. Apply the following rules in their numbered priority, preserving arrival order within each queue.
2. An exact REVERSED status wins queue 0, then hold_flag true wins queue 1. Neither branch examines amount_txt or invoice_day_txt. Status null, empty, different case and surrounding spaces do not qualify as terminal.
3. Only remaining rows inspect invoice_day_txt. Null, empty or whitespace-only means unknown invoice date. Otherwise trim, require exactly yyyy-MM-dd with two-digit month/day, and verify a real calendar date in UTC. Impossible dates and differently shaped dates go to defective queue 5, even when an amount or priority would otherwise qualify.
4. For a valid known invoice date, overdue means strictly before 2026-01-01. Such a row wins queue 2 without reading its amount, including malformed amount text. January 1 itself is not overdue; unknown invoice dates are not overdue.
5. After the preceding checks, trim amount_txt. Null/blank means zero. A nonblank value must have an optional leading minus, one to six integer digits, and optionally one or two fractional digits. Any other shape, excessive precision or invalid text goes to queue 5, including urgent rows.
6. A successfully interpreted amount at least 10000 wins queue 3. Negative values never qualify. Other rows use queue 4, except an exact URGENT priority combined with a strictly positive amount also wins queue 3. Empty/null priority and zero/negative urgent amounts remain ordinary.
7. Unexpected errors while evaluating a row must be logged and routed to queue 5. Invalid business text may be classified explicitly or by a logged error path; neither silent dropping nor component abortion is allowed. The downstream defect Reformat obtains its reason from its own validation and does not need this Partition to add fields.
8. Every edge carries the original record, including raw strings, nullable due_at and insured_value. No output construction, input edits or cross-row state is needed. Duplicate payment identifiers, the initial terminal row and the last urgent row must all survive exactly once.

rubric.description: Overdue payment routing bypasses irrelevant amount defects

required.check: Partition contract: `getOutputPort()` returns exactly one port index 0–5 for every record and leaves the record unchanged (no SKIP, ALL or output construction).
required.rationale: Returning SKIP or ALL drops or duplicates a payment that must reach exactly one queue.

required.check: Status test first, exactly: `status_cd == "REVERSED"` (null-safe, no trim or case folding) returns 0; then `hold_flag` true returns 1; both are decided before `invoice_day_txt` or `amount_txt` is read.
required.rationale: Trimming/upper-casing sends ' reversed ' to terminal; reading text first lets defects displace the decision.

required.check: A null, empty or whitespace-only `invoice_day_txt` is treated as unknown: not defective (not 5), not overdue, and the row continues to the amount rules.
required.rationale: Routing blank dates to 5 sends ordinary rows to the defect queue.

required.check: A nonblank date is trimmed and checked for exact `yyyy-MM-dd` shape with two-digit month and day by an explicit full-string check (e.g. regex `[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}`); any other shape (e.g. `2026-1-1`) returns 5.
required.rationale: Lenient parsing accepts single-digit month/day or trailing text that the clause sends to the defect queue.

required.check: An impossible calendar date (e.g. `2025-02-30`) returns 5: either strict `isDate(s,"yyyy-MM-dd",...,true)` false → 5, or strict `str2date(...,true)` throwing into a `getOutputPortOnError` that logs and returns 5.
required.rationale: Lenient parsing rolls 2025-02-30 into March and misroutes it as overdue.

required.check: The invoice date is fully classified before `amount_txt` is examined: a defective date returns 5 even with a high or urgent amount, and an overdue date returns 2 even when the amount text is malformed.
required.rationale: Checking the amount first lets a lower-priority defect displace the overdue or defect decision.

required.check: A valid date strictly before 2026-01-01 returns 2, comparing both dates in the same timezone (e.g. UTC parse vs `createDate(2026,1,1,"UTC")`, or comparing the `yyyy-MM-dd` text); 2026-01-01 itself is not overdue.
required.rationale: Using <= or mixed timezones moves the January 1 boundary.

required.check: After the date rules, a null or blank `amount_txt` (after trim) is treated as zero, not as a defect.
required.rationale: Routing blank amounts to 5 sends ordinary rows to the defect queue.

required.check: A nonblank trimmed amount must match optional minus, 1–6 integer digits, optionally a dot and 1–2 fractional digits (e.g. `-?[0-9]{1,6}(\.[0-9]{1,2})?`), checked explicitly before conversion; otherwise return 5 (e.g. `1000000`, `1.234`).
required.rationale: str2decimal accepts seven-digit or three-decimal text, so without a shape check those rows reach the value queues.

required.check: An interpreted amount `>= 10000` returns 3 (10000 inclusive); negative amounts never qualify by value.
required.rationale: Using > misses the 10000 boundary row.

required.check: Exact `priority_cd == "URGENT"` with amount strictly greater than 0 returns 3; zero or negative urgent amounts and null/empty priority return 4.
required.rationale: Ignoring the positivity condition sends zero-value urgent rows to review.

required.check: `getOutputPortOnError(string, string)` is implemented, logs the error (e.g. `printLog(error, ...)`), and returns 5.
required.rationale: Without it an unexpected error aborts the component; without logging it is silently routed.

forbidden.check: Parses `invoice_day_txt` and builds the 2026-01-01 cutoff in different timezones (e.g. `str2date` without "UTC" vs `createDate(...,"UTC")`), or uses `today()` as the cutoff.
forbidden.rationale: A CET-parsed 2026-01-01 is 2025-12-31T23:00Z and lands in the overdue queue.

forbidden.check: Writes to `$out`/modifies `$in` fields or keeps cross-row state to make the routing decision.
forbidden.rationale: Every edge must carry the original record, and routing is per-row (clause 8).

rubric_notes: Clause 5 says 'at most six integer digits' but the reference requires 1–6 (so '.5' is rejected); graded per the reference — consider rewording the prompt to 'one through six'. Fixture has no duplicate payment_key (reviewer advisory).

Cold-chain gaps outrank temperature alarms

A refrigerated carrier streams observations to a stateful Partition. The graph guarantees contiguous trips and numeric sample ordering, but disabled devices and malformed readings remain in the stream for operational accounting. The missing-sample queue is investigated separately from temperature alarms, and the same observation cannot be sent to both teams. Source metadata is carried unchanged to every downstream queue.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. A refrigeration monitor routes each sample unchanged to one of five queues: 0 disabled sensors, 1 faulty measurement text, 2 missing samples, 3 alarm and 4 normal. Samples are sorted into contiguous trip_id groups and increasing sample_no; duplicate numbers are allowed and keep their arrival order. Upstream validation guarantees sample_no is an integer from 0 through 1000000000, so gaps are measured within that bounded counter domain.
2. The first record of each trip establishes fresh state: there is no previous valid temperature or sample number. Trip IDs are exact case-sensitive text. Zero degrees and sample number zero are valid readings.
3. sensor_off true routes to queue 0 without inspecting temperature_txt. Disabled rows do not update the previous-valid baseline, even when their supplied temperature is well formed or the sample number is far ahead.
4. For active sensors, null, empty and trimmed-empty text routes to faulty queue 1. Otherwise accept exactly an optional minus, one or two integer digits, and optionally one fractional digit. Out-of-shape text also goes to 1; a valid parsed temperature must be between -50 and 50 inclusive or is faulty. Faulty rows leave the baseline unchanged.
5. Compare a valid sample to the preceding valid sample in the same trip. If a baseline exists and current sample_no exceeds its number by more than one, choose missing-sample queue 2, even if temperature would trigger an alarm. A duplicate sample number is not a gap.
6. If no gap wins, alarm queue 3 applies when temperature is above 8, below -20, or differs from the preceding valid temperature by more than 5 degrees in either direction. Threshold equality is safe. Without a predecessor only the absolute limits apply; remaining valid samples use queue 4.
7. Every valid active sample becomes the new baseline after its destination is decided, including a gap or alarm sample. Updating before comparison is incorrect. A following valid duplicate is compared with the immediately preceding valid sample, rather than an earlier record of the same numeric index.
8. Unexpected exceptions must be logged and reach faulty queue 1; they must not advance valid-state history. All source attributes including shipment_value, sample_time, notes and archive labels pass through. Keep all rows, including trip singletons and duplicate sample numbers, in per-queue arrival order.

required.check: Partition contract: `getOutputPort()` returns exactly one port 0–4 per record, keeping per-trip state in global variables.
required.rationale: Returning SKIP or keeping no state cannot implement gap and delta rules.

required.check: On a change of `trip_id` (exact, case-sensitive `!=` against the stored trip; with or without an extra first-record flag) the seen-valid state is reset so the trip starts with no predecessor, tracked by an explicit boolean (or equivalent explicit indicator, not a value of the temperature or sample number).
required.rationale: Carrying the previous trip's baseline creates false gaps and delta alarms on the first sample of a new trip.

required.check: `sensor_off` true returns 0 before `temperature_txt` is read.
required.rationale: Parsing first sends a disabled sensor with bad text to the faulty queue.

required.check: For an active sensor, null, empty or whitespace-only `temperature_txt` returns 1.
required.rationale: Treating blank as 0 degrees produces a valid baseline from no data.

required.check: Nonblank text must match optional minus, 1–2 integer digits, optionally one fractional digit (e.g. `-?[0-9]{1,2}(\.[0-9])?` on the trimmed text), else 1; the check runs before conversion.
required.rationale: str2decimal accepts '8.25' or '100', which the grammar sends to faulty.

required.check: A parsed temperature outside -50..50 inclusive returns 1.
required.rationale: Missing the range check lets out-of-range readings become alarms and baselines.

required.check: With a predecessor, `sample_no - prevNo > 1` returns 2, decided before any alarm test; a duplicate sample number (difference 0) or the next number is not a gap.
required.rationale: Testing alarms first sends a gap sample with an alarm temperature to queue 3.

required.check: Absolute alarm: temperature `> 8` or `< -20` returns 3 (strict, so 8 and -20 are normal); it applies also to the first valid sample of a trip.
required.rationale: Using >= alarms on the safe threshold values.

required.check: Delta alarm: only when a predecessor exists, `abs(t - prevTemp) > 5` returns 3 (a 5-degree change is normal).
required.rationale: Comparing against an unset baseline (0) raises a false delta alarm on the trip's first sample.

required.check: Every valid active sample (including those routed to 2 or 3) updates the baseline number, temperature and seen-valid flag after the port is decided, so the next sample compares with the immediately preceding valid one.
required.rationale: Updating before comparing compares a sample with itself; skipping the update on gap/alarm compares with a stale sample.

required.check: `getOutputPortOnError(string, string)` is implemented, logs the error, returns 1, and does not update the baseline.
required.rationale: An unlogged or missing error port either aborts the graph or advances history on a broken row.

forbidden.check: Uses a null test (`== null`/`isnull`) on a declared integer/decimal, or the value 0, as the 'no previous valid sample' sentinel.
forbidden.rationale: Declared scalars start at 0, never null, and 0 degrees / sample 0 are valid baselines.

forbidden.check: Updates the previous-valid baseline (number, temperature or flag) on a disabled (port 0) or faulty (port 1) row.
forbidden.rationale: Disabled and faulty rows must leave the baseline unchanged (clauses 3–4).

Invoice utilities round once after the surcharge

An invoice loader applies a reusable CTL library through a Reformat wrapper. Monetary fields are already typed, and the application wants displayed identifiers, payable amounts and signed budget shares without losing original inputs. Output has to be independent of runtime timezone. The supplied ports are the wrapper metadata; no graph resources participate.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Provide exactly four port-independent reusable functions named canonicalCode(string value), pricedAmount(decimal gross, decimal pct, decimal surcharge), budgetShare(decimal amount, decimal budget), and businessToken(string code, date value). They must use no mutable global state; the Reformat wrapper invokes them for every invoice.
2. canonicalCode returns null for null, otherwise trims surrounding whitespace and uppercases. Empty and whitespace-only remain empty strings. Internal spaces and delimiter characters are ordinary data, with no code validation or replacement sentinel.
3. pricedAmount returns null if gross or pct is null. A null surcharge means zero, independently of those required arguments. Otherwise its unrounded value is gross*(100-pct)/100+surcharge; round exactly once at the final result to two places, halves away from zero, never round the discount part before adding the surcharge.
4. Business input bounds are gross and surcharge from -1000000 to 1000000 and pct from -1000 to 1000, all at two fractional places. Negative gross, surcharge and percentages and pct above 100 remain allowed. Do not clamp, take absolute values or convert monetary calculation to floating point.
5. budgetShare returns null when amount or budget is null; null takes precedence over zero. A non-null zero budget returns exactly 0.00 even when amount is nonzero. Otherwise return amount/budget*100 rounded to two places with halves away from zero, retaining a negative sign where the ratio is negative.
6. businessToken returns null when either code or value is null; otherwise concatenate canonicalCode(code), a slash and the UTC calendar date yyyy-MM-dd. Empty code keeps the slash. Midnight dates are valid, and input date values must not be changed or formatted in the host timezone.
7. The wrapper copies all original invoice attributes. clean_code comes from raw_code; net_amount uses gross_amount, discount_percent and surcharge_amount; budget_pct uses the resulting net_amount and budget_amount, not gross; business_token uses raw_code and document_dt.
8. Every source row emits one record in arrival order, including duplicates and any combination of null arguments. First and final invoices follow identical function contracts. The notes, raw code, decimal inputs and unused archive label must remain exactly as read; no sequence, cache or external resource is available.

required.check: A null surcharge is treated as zero (e.g. `nvl(surcharge, 0D)`), independently of the null rule for gross and pct.

Meter utility distinguishes malformed text from absent readings

A utilities gateway uses the same four CTL functions from several ingestion graphs. This task supplies their Reformat consumer with raw meter strings; malformed firmware readings remain audit rows instead of throwing away the source record. The library classifies missing, malformed and reset readings independently of operational meter status. Decimal formatting for labels must remain stable across locale settings.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The shared library exports exactly four pure functions: readingValue(string text), readingDelta(string newer, string older), deltaStatus(string newer, string older), and readingLabel(string unit, string text). Port access belongs only to the surrounding Reformat. These functions carry no history between calls.
2. readingValue returns null for null, empty and whitespace-only input. Trim nonblank text and accept only an optional minus, one through five digits, and optionally a dot plus one or two fractional digits. Accepted zero and negative values become decimal values; a leading plus, comma, exponent, too many digits or excessive fractional precision instead yields null without throwing.
3. readingDelta parses each argument under that same contract. Return null if either argument lacks a valid numeric value, otherwise newer minus older, retaining negative consumption deltas. Do not turn a missing old reading into zero and do not round individual parsed values.
4. deltaStatus gives NEW_BAD when newer is nonblank but invalid. This outranks any older defect. Otherwise a nonblank invalid older gives OLD_BAD, even if newer is missing. Missing here means null or trimmed-empty, while malformed nonblank is a separate condition.
5. If neither malformed-text rule applies, deltaStatus gives MISSING when either side is missing; otherwise RESET for a negative delta, SAME for zero delta and ADVANCE for a positive delta. Numerical zero must remain present rather than being used as a missing sentinel.
6. readingLabel returns null if unit is null or text has no valid reading. Otherwise uppercase the trimmed unit, append a colon and render readingValue(text) in en.US with exactly two fractional digits and no grouping. An empty/whitespace unit stays empty before the colon; internal unit whitespace is retained.
7. The wrapper copies every source attribute and assigns current_value from current_text, delta_value and delta_status from current_text/previous_text, and reading_label from unit_code/current_text. meter_status, calibration_factor and captured_at are informational and must not affect interpretation.
8. Emit each source row, including first/last and duplicates, in arrival order even for malformed text. All four public functions must give the same result when invoked independently by a different graph. Preserve raw numeric strings, dates, null notes and the unused archive field unchanged.

Order fixtures alternate discounts per customer

An order assertion graph runs this DataGenerator in UTC and writes generated line items to a reconciliation collector. It sets a finite component row count from FIXTURE_ROWS before execution. The fixture retains three-line customer relationships while adding realistic discounted totals and a subtotal that must carry across calls within one customer and reset before the next. No external sequences, random source or live clock are available.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The DataGenerator has no input and one connected output. Graph parameter FIXTURE_ROWS defaults to 8 and the component already has recordsNumber=${FIXTURE_ROWS}; allowed counts are 0 through 20. Generate exactly that configured population.
2. Use one-based source row n beginning at 1. fixture_id is 100000+n, customer_id is 1000 plus the integer quotient (n-1)/3, and line_no is (n-1)%3+1. Incomplete final triples remain valid. fixture_row is n as a long, and each generated identifier must agree with the same row number.
3. unit_price is 12.50 plus line_no and quantity equals line_no. The first customer uses discount_pct 0, the next 10, then 0, alternating by zero-based customer index rather than by individual line. Discounts apply to every line of the same customer.
4. line_total is unit_price*quantity*(100-discount_pct)/100, using decimal arithmetic and half-up rounding to two places. Never derive the total by parsing text or by integer percentage division. Negative or random fixture prices are not part of this scenario.
5. customer_total is the running sum of already rounded line totals within this customer, including the current line. It restarts with each customer.
6. event_dt is UTC midnight 2026-01-01 plus n-1 calendar days; fixture_received is the same instant. fixture_state is OPEN for odd n and CLOSED for even n, independent of customer discount. A one-row run begins on January 1 with OPEN.
7. Set fixture_key to FIX- followed by fixture_id in ordinary base-10, fixture_trace to CUST- followed by customer_id, fixture_tenant TEST, fixture_file synthetic, fixture_currency EUR and fixture_batch FIXTURE. Explicitly assign fixture_team, fixture_market, fixture_note and fixture_unused_archive null on every row.
8. The row numbering runs across customers; it does not restart at customer boundaries.

The receiving assertion collector checks that capacity clipping changes the next step’s starting state and that accumulated spill persists through later empty storage. This is a synthetic mathematical fixture with no reader or external resource state.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. A reservoir regression graph provides this DataGenerator no input and one output. STEPS defaults to 9 and already controls the component recordsNumber; it is an integer from 0 to 20. Each requested step emits one row; zero requested steps emits none.
2. The simulation starts with 5.00 units stored before step 1. step_no and tank_row are one-based. prior_level is the previous step’s stored_level, with exactly 5.00 for the first row. A stored zero is real state; never reinitialize merely because the previous level is zero.

6. level_band is EMPTY when stored_level equals zero, FULL when it equals ten, otherwise PARTIAL. Threshold equality must select the boundary bands.

Receipt audit identities use framed business tuples

An append-only receipt audit graph puts this Reformat before its ledger writer. Orchestration parameters carry the run identity and file name, while AuditRows provides long row identifiers independently of the business digest. The audit comparison tool treats null, empty text and delimiter-bearing references as distinct selected tuples. Records with a repeated business identity still represent separate source arrivals.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The orchestration supplies AUDIT_RUN_ID, RUN_TS and SOURCE_FILE graph parameters; example values are R2-A, 2026-01-05 08:00:00 and receipts.csv. Read current parameter values into run_id and audit_source. Parse RUN_TS as a strict UTC yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss timestamp into run_ts; do not overwrite receipt_file.
2. The digest tuple is merchant_cd, transaction_ref, posted_amount and posting_dt, in that order. A null component is represented by N. Each non-null string is V followed by exact original text, including empty strings, surrounding whitespace, colons and pipes; trimming or case folding would change identity.
3. A non-null amount is V followed by en.US fixed two-decimal text without grouping, rounded half-up if needed. Input amounts are within +/-1000000. A non-null posting date is V followed by its UTC yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss representation, with explicit midnight time when appropriate.
4. Frame each represented part as its decimal CTL string length, a colon and the entire represented part. Length includes the marker and counts UTF-16 code units. Concatenate all four frames with no additional separator. A delimiter inside a string is data, never a boundary.
5. record_digest is lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of that complete framed string. Equivalent supported hash/hex conversions are valid. Null merchant and empty merchant must differ. Duplicate selected tuples must produce the same digest even when their receipt context or audit sequence differs.
6. A graph-managed sequence AuditRows begins at 1 with step 1 and must be accessed as long. Each source row consumes exactly one next value into audit_seq during record transformation, including duplicate tuples. Do not reset the sequence or read it during initialization/shutdown.
7. Copy all original fields unchanged, including original filename, timestamps, exact text inputs, nullable receipt_note and receipt_unused_archive. The new audit_source names the orchestration source; it does not alter any original source attribute.
8. Emit one output per input in source order and retain the first, final and duplicate rows. No digest cache may suppress rows or suppress sequence consumption. Any unexpected hashing error must fail visibly rather than silently acknowledge a missing audit record.

Claims audit keeps history only for accepted requests

An insurer’s audit Reformat reads its run configuration from typed graph dictionary entries. It receives every claim, including records that opted out, and appends audit decisions without changing source attributes. The accepted sequence and monetary total belong only to this component execution, rather than an external sequence. Disabled auditing must be safe even when a timestamp or the otherwise unused cutoff text is malformed.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The graph dictionary supplies auditEnabled boolean true, auditLabel string CLAIMS-R2, and cutoffText string 2026-01-01 00:00:00. These entries may change between runs. Dictionary auditEnabled is the run-level switch, while audit_requested is each row’s request; neither substitutes for the other.
2. If auditing is disabled for the run or not requested by this row, emit audit_state BYPASS, audit_label null, accepted_at null, accepted_index zero, accepted_running equal to the current accepted monetary total, and previous_claim_key null. Do not inspect submitted_txt or parse cutoffText on this branch.
3. For a requested enabled row, submitted_txt must be present and match exactly yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss before strict UTC calendar parsing. Null, blank, impossible dates and different shapes yield audit_state BAD_TIME, null accepted_at and previous_claim_key, index zero and the unchanged running total. These are ordinary output records, not thrown errors.
4. Parse dictionary cutoffText strictly in UTC only when a row reaches valid submission-time evaluation. It is guaranteed valid when auditing is enabled. A submitted timestamp before the cutoff yields audit_state TOO_OLD with the same nonaccepted outputs as BAD_TIME; equality is accepted.
5. An accepted row emits audit_state ACCEPTED and its parsed submitted time into accepted_at. accepted_index counts only accepted records, one-based across the whole stream. Rejected/bypassed rows do not consume an index or advance accepted-history state.
6. claimed_amount may be null, zero or negative within +/-1000000; null contributes zero to the accepted running total. Add the current accepted amount before emitting accepted_running. For every nonaccepted row preserve the total already accumulated, including when it is zero.
7. previous_claim_key is null on the first accepted record; otherwise it is the exact claim_key from the immediately preceding accepted record, skipping all intervening nonaccepted rows. Empty claim_key is allowed and must be remembered as a valid prior key.
8. audit_label equals the current dictionary label on enabled/requested rows, including BAD_TIME and TOO_OLD, but remains null on bypasses. Copy every original claim field unchanged; emit every source row in arrival order, retain duplicates and do not reorder claims by parsed timestamp.
9. A new component execution starts accepted index and monetary total at zero with no preceding accepted key. Dictionary entries are read-only configuration and must never be mutated to store counters. Unexpected errors after business guards must fail visibly or log before propagating; no silent skipping is permitted.
